simple.meaning: יֶלֶק (yeleq) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a devourer ; specifically, the young locust.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Psalms 105:34. The surrounding context includes land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יֶלֶק (H3218) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: יֶלֶק (yeleq) / H3218 is traced through Psalms 105:34, Jeremiah 51:14, Jeremiah 51:27, Joel 1:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: He spoke, and the locusts came
Yahweh of Armies has sworn by himself, saying,
“Set up a standard in the land!
What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten.
What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten.
I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten,
There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips, and flees away.

definitions.full: H3218. yeleq יֶ֫לֶק noun masculine Nahum 3:16 a kind of locust , absolute יֶלֶק 3:16 5 t.; יָ֑לֶק Joel 1:4 2 t.; — always collective: a. as devouring || חָסִיל אַרְבֶּה, גָּזָם, , Joel 1:4 (twice in verse); 2:25 ; || אַרְבֶּה Psa 105:34 (of Egyptian plague), compare Nahum 3:15 a (but strike out We). b. in simile of multitude of men Nahum 3:15 b Jer 51:14 ; of horses 51:27 ( סָמָר יֶלֶק ). c. in simile of scattering and disappearing Nahum 3:16 . יַלְקוּט see לקט .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to lick up;
